name: District 1
summary: Ho Chi Minh City's central visitor base: hotels, landmarks, malls, rooftop bars, tour pickups, and dense traffic.
description: District 1 is the easiest first base in Ho Chi Minh City, with most classic sights, restaurants, cocktail bars, and tour departures close together. It is convenient rather than quiet, and tourist pricing is common around major landmarks.

name: District 3
summary: A central but more lived-in district with leafy streets, cafes, local restaurants, and easier daily rhythm than District 1.
description: District 3 sits close to District 1 but feels more residential and local. It works well for travelers who want central access without sleeping in the most tourist-heavy core.

name: Thao Dien
summary: An expat-leaning riverside area with international schools, villas, coworking-friendly cafes, restaurants, and a calmer long-stay feel.
description: Thao Dien is popular with expats and longer-stay visitors. It is less convenient for classic sightseeing but strong for cafes, gyms, family routines, and international food.

name: Binh Thanh
summary: A mixed residential district between central Saigon and Thao Dien, with local food streets, apartments, and high-rise pockets.
description: Binh Thanh blends everyday local life with newer apartment towers and riverfront views. It can be good value, but traffic and walkability vary block by block.

name: Cho Lon
summary: The city's historic Chinese-Vietnamese commercial area, with markets, temples, herbal shops, and dense local street life.
description: Cho Lon rewards patient exploration and is less polished than central tourist zones. It is best approached respectfully, with attention to market flow, temple etiquette, and traffic.

name: Old Quarter
summary: Hanoi's dense historic visitor core: narrow streets, food stalls, shops, hostels, boutique hotels, and constant street movement.
description: The Old Quarter is atmospheric and convenient, but noise, traffic, touts, and small sidewalks are part of the daily texture. It is the easiest base for first-time sightseeing.

name: French Quarter
summary: A more formal central area with wider streets, colonial-era architecture, embassies, museums, and higher-end hotels.
description: The French Quarter is calmer and more polished than the Old Quarter, with a stronger hotel, museum, and restaurant rhythm.

name: Tay Ho
summary: A lakefront expat and long-stay district with cafes, apartments, international restaurants, gyms, and slower daily routines.
description: Tay Ho is less useful for first-time sightseeing but strong for longer stays, remote work, and calmer evenings around West Lake.

name: Ba Dinh
summary: A formal government and history district with museums, monuments, embassies, and quieter streets than the Old Quarter.
description: Ba Dinh has a more official tone. Travelers should be especially careful around government buildings, ceremonies, and security areas.

name: My Khe & An Thuong
summary: Da Nang's main traveler beach zone, with surf-facing hotels, cafes, casual bars, seafood, and an international long-stay feel.
description: The My Khe and An Thuong area is practical for beach-focused travelers and remote workers. It is easier and more relaxed than Vietnam's biggest city cores.

name: Hai Chau
summary: Da Nang's central urban district, with river bridges, markets, offices, local restaurants, and transport convenience.
description: Hai Chau is more city-life than beach-life. It works for practical access, food, and local errands, while beach travelers may prefer the east side.

name: Ancient Town
summary: Hoi An's walkable heritage core, with lantern streets, tailor shops, cafes, ticketed sights, and heavy evening visitor flows.
description: Ancient Town is beautiful and very visitor-oriented. It is best enjoyed early or late with patience for crowds and respect for homes, temples, and heritage buildings.

name: An Bang
summary: A relaxed beach village area with guesthouses, seafood restaurants, casual bars, and easier pacing than the old town.
description: An Bang is a good balance for travelers who want Hoi An access without sleeping inside the densest heritage crowds.
